change: OriginalStateRecord keeps records of at least 0x400000 bytes (only the 0x630e18-byte replay recording/playback buffers today) in 16 KiB pages ([[UInt8]]/[[Bool]]). bytes/defined became computed: a paged record assembles them once per written version into a lock-protected cache shared by copies with the same contents; every write starts a new cache. byteCount was added; == compares contents. Per-cycle storage.bytes.count reads (replay range check, menu/pool reserve loops, catalog ranges) use byteCount. The replay writer reads its source once without caching (readOnce) and takes the compressed prefix with leadingBytes, so freed buffers keep no assembled copy. Test helpers: two .bytes.count reads use byteCount; the launch comparison reads each record's arrays once per call. Three more test comparison helpers (LoadedCharacterComparison.equal/transition, GameplayStateProjection.same) read each record's arrays once per call.
why: each game cycle works on rollback copies (var candidate = state ... state = candidate); the replay packet write duplicated the whole buffer (1,659 copies of 6.5 MB plus mask per match on macOS; 16.1% of the phone's time in memcpy under OriginalStateRecord.write<Int8>)
